# Microscopic jamming in the negative spherical perceptron

Coordinate `EN-115-000-0020-2-2026-PR-T4-UK-EX-M2-B-PH-M-0430` | `PM-222.2` | status ACTIVE | original slug `Microscopic-jamming-in-the-negative-spherical-perceptron-September-24-2026` | date 2026-09-24 | derived from the openai/math preprint Microscopic-jamming-in-the-negative-spherical-perceptron-September-24-2026, modified (Apache-2.0). ```json
{
  "abstract_verbatim": "We prove a sharp feasibility threshold and limiting gap and force laws for the spherical perceptron with margin −1 and quadratic penalty. The limits are taken successively in system size, inverse temperature, and density approaching the threshold from above. They agree for Gaussian coordinates and for the equal mixture of centered Gaussian coordinates with variances $`1-\\varepsilon`$ and $`1+\\varepsilon`$, for every sufficiently small fixed <i>ε</i>. The contact-removed gap cumulative law and the mean-one force cumulative law satisfy\n\n$`\\displaystyle G_J(u)=u^{1-\\gamma+o(1)},\\qquad F_J(s)=s^{1+\\theta+o(1)},`$\n\nas $`u\\downarrow0`$ and $`s\\downarrow0`$, with $`\\gamma=(2+\\theta)^{-1}`$, $`0.4126930\\lt \\gamma\\lt 0.4126934`$, and $`0.4231063\\lt \\theta\\lt 0.4231088`$. A finite numerical certificate for these exponent intervals, together with its mathematical error bounds, is included.",

<a id="pm-s1"></a>
## 1. Abstract and result contract

> We prove a sharp feasibility threshold and limiting gap and force laws for the spherical perceptron with margin −1 and quadratic penalty. The limits are taken successively in system size, inverse temperature, and density approaching the threshold from above. They agree for Gaussian coordinates and for the equal mixture of centered Gaussian coordinates with variances $`1-\varepsilon`$ and $`1+\varepsilon`$, for every sufficiently small fixed <i>ε</i>. The contact-removed gap cumulative law and the mean-one force cumulative law satisfy
> 
> $`\displaystyle G_J(u)=u^{1-\gamma+o(1)},\qquad F_J(s)=s^{1+\theta+o(1)},`$
> 
> as $`u\downarrow0`$ and $`s\downarrow0`$, with $`\gamma=(2+\theta)^{-1}`$, $`0.4126930\lt \gamma\lt 0.4126934`$, and $`0.4231063\lt \theta\lt 0.4231088`$. A finite numerical certificate for these exponent intervals, together with its mathematical error bounds, is included.

- **claim-microscopic-criticality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-main)): There exist $\alpha_c\in(0,\infty)$ and $\varepsilon_0\in(0,1)$ with the following properties for every fixed $\varepsilon\in[0,\varepsilon_0)$ and coordinate law $\nu_\varepsilon$.* 1. *The SAT probability tends to one at every fixed $\alpha<\alpha_c$ and to zero at every fixed $\alpha>\alpha_c$.* 2. *All the ordered limits in <a href="#eq:intro-GJ" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:intro-GJ">[eq:intro-GJ]</a>–<a href="#eq:intro-FJ" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:intro-FJ">[eq:intro-FJ]</a> exist for their indicated positive arguments. They are independent of $\varepsilon$.* 3. *$F_J$ is the cumulative distribution function on $(0,\infty)$ of a probability law of mean one. It has no atom at zero. There are exponents $\gamma,\theta$ such that $$G_J(u)=u^{1-\gamma+o(1)},\qquad F_J(s)=s^{1+\theta+o(1)},$$ as the corresponding argument decreases to zero, and $$\gamma=\frac1{2+\theta},\qquad 0.4126930<\gamma<0.4126934,\qquad 0.4231063<\theta<0.4231088.$$
  - Explanation: A common sharp feasibility threshold and ordered critical gap and force laws hold for Gaussian coordinates and sufficiently small fixed independent Gaussian variance mixtures. The cumulative exponents satisfy the stated exact relation and certified enclosures.
- **claim-cascade-change-of-measure** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-cascade-tilt)): For a fixed finite cascade, $0<T<\infty$ almost surely and $\mathbb E\|\log T\|^2<\infty$. Attach marks to its vertices, independently of the Poisson processes, with conditionally independent and identically distributed child marks given the ancestral marks. A terminal function $X_\tau$ of the path marks determines recursive functions by $$X_v=\frac1{m_{j-1}}\log \mathbb E\bigl[\exp(m_{j-1}X_{vi})\mid\text{marks up to }v\bigr] \quad\text{at depth }j-1. \label{eq:hier-mark-recursion}$$ Suppose these moments are finite and $\mathbb E\|X_\varnothing\|<\infty$. Reweighting the leaf probabilities by $e^{X_\tau}$ preserves the law of their genealogy. Conditional on the transformed genealogy, the child-mark transition at depth $j$ is multiplied by $$\exp\{m_{j-1}(X_{vi}-X_v)\}. \label{eq:hier-child-tilt}$$ Root marks retain their original distribution. Moreover, $$\mathbb E\log\sum_\tau v_\tau e^{X_\tau}=\mathbb EX_\varnothing. \label{eq:hier-root-expectation}$$ If the marks are independent families and $X_\tau$ is the sum of one function of each family, both the recursion and the tilted path law factor over the families, including conditional on the genealogy of finitely many replicas.
  - Explanation: The finite cascade normalizes almost surely. Exponential reweighting preserves its genealogy while changing the conditional mark transitions; independent mark families retain their conditional factorization.
- **claim-continuous-rank-array** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-rank-array)): For two independent samples from a depth-$k$ cascade, the probability that their leaves share exactly $j$ edges is $w_j$, $0\le j\le k$; sharing $k$ edges includes selecting the same leaf. There exists a weakly exchangeable ultrametric array $(U_{ab})_{a,b\ge1}$ with $U_{aa}=1$ and $U_{12}$ uniform on $[0,1]$, such that every step-profile cascade covariance array has law $$C_{aa}=Q,\qquad C_{ab}=q(U_{ab})\quad(a\ne b).$$ All the finite-dimensional laws of this rank array are determined by its nested partition sampling rule.
  - Explanation: Cascade sampling probabilities admit a common continuous ultrametric rank representation. The diagonal covariance remains separate from the off-diagonal profile.
- **claim-replica-array-continuity** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-array-continuity)): Let $G_n$ be random probability measures. Suppose that the jointly sampled arrays of a finite list of uniformly bounded positive-semidefinite kernels, and any other bounded observables being retained, converge in law on every finite set of replicas. Conditional on these arrays, adjoin independent centered Gaussian fields with the prescribed kernels. Let $X_n$ be the evaluation of one fixed continuous function on the retained single-replica variables and those fields, and assume, for every fixed $a>0$, $$\sup_n\mathbb EG_n(e^{a\|X_n\|})<\infty. \label{eq:hier-exponential-moments}$$ Then the expectations of $\log G_n(e^{X_n})$, and the expectations of bounded continuous functions of finitely many replicas sampled from $e^{X_n}G_n/G_n(e^{X_n})$, converge to the corresponding functionals of the limiting array. Independent auxiliary variables of a fixed law may be adjoined to each replica. The conclusion also holds for unbounded observables whose truncation errors vanish uniformly under the tilted law; in particular this follows for polynomial functions of the Gaussian fields under <a href="#eq:hier-exponential-moments" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:hier-exponential-moments">[eq:hier-exponential-moments]</a>.
  - Explanation: Finite-replica convergence passes through Gaussian tilting when the required uniform exponential moments hold. Unbounded observables additionally require uniformly vanishing truncation errors.
- **claim-row-profile-interpolation** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-hier-row-interpolation)): For a step profile define $D_q(s)=\mathbb EA_j^2$ on $[m_{j-1},m_j)$. This is nonnegative and nondecreasing, satisfies $D_q\le\\|u'\\|_\infty^2$, and is constant across adjacent equal values of $q$. The diagonal quantity $D_{q,d}:=\mathbb E^{\mathrm{tilt}}u'(Z)^2$ is at least the final off-diagonal value. For two profiles with common diagonal $Q$, $$\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\Phi_u((1-t)q+tr;Q) =-\frac12\int_0^1(r-q)(s)D_{(1-t)q+tr}(s)\,\mathrm ds. \label{eq:src1}$$ For arbitrary $q,r\in\mathcal Q_Q$ this identity holds for $0<t<1$ and as the appropriate one-sided derivative at the endpoints. Moreover, $$\|\Phi_u(q;Q)-\Phi_u(r;Q)\| \le\frac12\\|u'\\|_\infty^2\\|q-r\\|_1, \qquad q\longmapsto D_q\text{ is continuous into }L^1[0,1]. \label{eq:hier-row-continuity}$$ For a general profile, $D_q$ is constant almost everywhere on every interval on which $q$ is constant almost everywhere.
  - Explanation: The tilted derivative martingale defines a bounded monotone derivative profile. Gaussian interpolation gives the row-functional derivative, continuity, and plateau preservation.
- **claim-explicit-spherical-entropy** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-hier-spherical-limit)): The limit $\mathcal S(p)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathcal S_N(p)$ exists and is uniform over all nonnegative nondecreasing profiles bounded by any fixed constant. For a finite-step profile without residual diagonal, put $$\Delta p_j=p_j-p_{j-1},\qquad I=\sum_{j=1}^k m_{j-1}\Delta p_j, \qquad \lambda_j=b-\sum_{i=j+1}^k m_{i-1}\Delta p_i\quad(0\le j\le k).$$ Thus $\lambda_k=b$, $\lambda_0=b-I$, and $\lambda_{j-1}=\lambda_j-m_{j-1}\Delta p_j$. Define, for $b>I$, $$X(b)=-\frac12\log b+\frac{p_0}{2\lambda_0} +\sum_{j=1}^k\frac1{2m_{j-1}} \log\frac{\lambda_j}{\lambda_{j-1}}. \label{eq:hier-gaussian-spin}$$ There is exactly one $b>I$ satisfying $$-2X'(b)=\frac1b+\frac{p_0}{\lambda_0^2} +\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{p_j-p_{j-1}}{\lambda_j\lambda_{j-1}}=1. \label{eq:src2}$$ At this value of $b$, $$\mathcal S(p)=X(b)+\frac b2-\frac12-\frac{p_k}{2}. \label{eq:hier-spherical-value}$$ If $p\le B$, its saddle point satisfies $1\le b<2(B+1)$.
  - Explanation: The spherical functional has a uniform thermodynamic limit on bounded monotone profiles. A unique scalar saddle point determines its explicit value for finite hierarchies.
- **claim-spherical-concavity-inverse-map** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-hier-spin-concavity)): The functional $\mathcal S$ is concave on bounded nonnegative nondecreasing profiles. At a finite-step profile its differential is $$\mathrm d\mathcal S(p)=-\frac12\sum_{j=0}^k w_jr_j\,\mathrm dp_j, \quad r_j=\frac{p_0}{\lambda_0^2} +\sum_{i=1}^j\frac{p_i-p_{i-1}}{\lambda_i\lambda_{i-1}}, \quad r_k=1-\frac1b. \label{eq:hier-spin-gradient}$$ For every general bounded profile $p$ there exists a nonnegative nondecreasing profile $r$, with $r_*<1$, such that $$\mathcal S(\widetilde p) \le\mathcal S(p)-\frac12\int_0^1r(s)(\widetilde p-p)(s)\,\mathrm ds \label{eq:hier-spin-tangent}$$ for every bounded nonnegative nondecreasing $\widetilde p$. The profile $r$ can be chosen so that $p=\mathcal I(r)$ almost everywhere. If $p\le B$, $r$ may be chosen with $r_*\le1-[2(B+1)]^{-1}$.
  - Explanation: The limiting spherical functional is concave. Its selected monotone supergradient is related to the covariance profile by the continuous inverse map.
- **claim-entropy-conjugacy** (construction, [source](#stmt-prop-hier-entropy-conjugacy)): Let $q$ be nonnegative and nondecreasing with $q_*<1$, and use $\chi_q$ defined above. Then the following supremum is attained: $$\begin{split} E(q)&:=\sup_{\substack{p\ge0\text{ bounded}\\p\text{ nondecreasing}}} \left\{\mathcal S(p)+\frac12\int_0^1q(s)p(s)\,\mathrm ds\right\}\\ &=\frac12\left\{\log(1-q_*)+ \int_0^{q_*}\frac{\mathrm dt}{\chi_q(t)}\right\}, \qquad \chi_q(t)=\int_t^1m_q(v)\,\mathrm dv. \end{split} \label{eq:src3}$$ An optimizer may be chosen with $p_*\le q_*/(1-q_*)^2$. Equivalently, $$E(q)=\frac12\int_0^1 \left\{\frac1{\chi_q(t)}-\frac1{1-t}\right\}\,\mathrm dt, \label{eq:hier-entropy-integral}$$ where the integrand is identically zero for $t>q_*$. For profiles $q,\widetilde q\le Q<1$, $$\|E(q)-E(\widetilde q)\| \le\frac{Q}{2(1-Q)^2}\\|q-\widetilde q\\|_1. \label{eq:hier-entropy-continuity}$$
  - Explanation: The spherical entropy conjugate is attained and equals the displayed susceptibility integral. Uniform separation from the endpoint gives quantitative continuity.
- **claim-parabolic-regularity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-conc-regularity)): Equation <a href="#eq:conc-variance-pde" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:conc-variance-pde">[eq:conc-variance-pde]</a> has a unique solution of at most quadratic growth with a spatial derivative of at most linear growth. For continuous $m:[0,Q]\to[0,1]$, the solution is classical and satisfies $$-C\leq F_{zz}(t,z)\leq\frac{\kappa}{1-\kappa(Q-t)}, \qquad \|F_z(t,z)\|\leq C_1(1+\|z\|). \label{eq:conc-parabolic-bounds}$$ For a fixed smooth terminal, each spatial derivative of order at least two is bounded. The corresponding bounds are uniform over $m\in[0,1]$. For a smooth profile $q$ with $\dot q>0$ and a smooth direction $\eta$ with $\eta(0)=\eta(1)=0$, the solution of <a href="#eq:src4" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src4">[eq:src4]</a> is twice differentiable in the parameter $\varepsilon$ at $q+\varepsilon\eta$.
  - Explanation: The row equation is well posed in its stated growth class. Uniform spatial curvature estimates support differentiation with respect to smooth covariance-profile variations.
- **claim-row-hessian-identity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-conc-hessian)): Set $\bar v=v+\eta U/2$ and $l=\bar v_z$. Then $$\begin{split} w(0,0)&=\mathbb E\int_0^1 \left(\dot q s l^2-2\eta a l-\frac12\eta^2b^2\right)\mathrm ds,\\ \mathcal Dl&=\eta a b-\dot q s b l,\qquad l(1,\cdot)=0. \end{split} \label{eq:src5}$$
  - Explanation: A modified profile variation removes the derivative of the variation direction from the Hessian formula and yields a linear terminal-value equation for its spatial derivative.
- **claim-row-functional-concavity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-conc-concavity)): For every concave terminal in the class <a href="#eq:conc-terminal-class" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:conc-terminal-class">[eq:conc-terminal-class]</a>, $q\mapsto\Phi_u(q;Q)$ is concave on smooth strictly increasing profiles. For every concave globally Lipschitz terminal, which need not be smooth or bounded above, and for the quadratic hinge $u=-\beta V$, it is concave on the full convex set of nonnegative nondecreasing profiles bounded by $Q$.
  - Explanation: Concave terminals produce concavity in the covariance profile. Approximation extends the result to globally Lipschitz concave terminals and the quadratic hinge.
- **claim-diffusion-density-control** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-conc-density)): Let $X$ solve $\mathrm dX_t=\mathrm dB_t+A(t,X_t)\mathrm dt$, with $\|\partial_zA\|\leq K$ and $\|A(t,0)\|\leq K$. Over an interval of length $T>0$, its transition density is bounded above by $e^{KT}/\sqrt{2\pi T}$. Moreover, when $X_0=0$, $Q\in[1/2,2]$, and $K$ is fixed, the probability $\mathbb P(X_Q\in I)$ is bounded below by a positive constant depending only on $K$ and the nondegenerate bounded interval $I$.
  - Explanation: A uniformly Lipschitz drift gives an explicit transition-density upper bound and a uniform positive probability of reaching a fixed nondegenerate interval.
- **claim-strict-concavity-stability** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-conc-stability)): There is $c_\beta>0$ such that, for every $Q\in[1/2,2]$, every regularized base terminal just described, every smooth strictly increasing profile, and every smooth endpoint-zero direction, $$\frac{\mathrm d^2}{\mathrm d\varepsilon^2} \Phi_u(q+\varepsilon\eta;Q)\big\|_{\varepsilon=0} \leq-c_\beta\\|\eta\\|_2^2. \label{eq:conc-strict-hessian}$$ For each $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$ there is $d_0=d_0(\beta,\psi)>0$, independent of $L$, $\delta$, $\lambda$, $Q$, and the profile, such that <a href="#eq:conc-strict-hessian" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:conc-strict-hessian">[eq:conc-strict-hessian]</a> holds with $c_\beta/2$ for the terminal $u+d\psi$ whenever $\|d\|\leq d_0$.
  - Explanation: The hinge curvature yields strict profile concavity uniformly over the regularizations and profiles. Small compact terminal perturbations retain a quantitative fraction of this bound.
- **claim-uncapped-hinge-stability** (bound, [source](#stmt-cor-conc-hinge-stability)): Fix $\beta>0$ and $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$. There are constants $c_\beta>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\beta,\psi)>0$ such that, for $u_d=-\beta V+d\psi$, $\|d\|\le d_0$, $Q\in[1/2,2]$, and all $q,r\in\mathcal Q_Q$, $$\Phi_{u_d}((1-t)q+tr;Q) \ge(1-t)\Phi_{u_d}(q;Q)+t\Phi_{u_d}(r;Q) +\frac{c_\beta}{4}t(1-t)\\|r-q\\|_2^2, \qquad 0\le t\le1. \label{eq:conc-chord}$$ When $d=0$, the last coefficient can be replaced by $c_\beta/2$. The derivative formula <a href="#eq:src1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src1">[eq:src1]</a>, including its one-sided endpoint interpretation, holds with the terminal $u_d$ and fixed diagonal $Q$. Its nonnegative nondecreasing derivative profile satisfies $\sup_{q,Q,d}\\|D^{u_d}_q\\|_\infty\le C_{\beta,\psi}$ in these ranges and depends continuously on $q$ in $L^1$ at fixed $Q,d$. The functional values and derivative profiles are limits of those for $u_{L,\delta}+d\psi$, uniformly over $q,Q,d$, with derivative convergence in $L^1(\mathrm ds)$. Here $\delta\downarrow0$ at each fixed cap before $L\to\infty$.
  - Explanation: Strong concavity and the derivative identity survive the ordered removal of mollification and tangent caps. The derivative profiles converge uniformly in the stated parameter ranges.
- **claim-convex-loss-cap-removal** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-conc-convex-loss)): Let $$W(z)=cV(z)+\chi(z),\qquad c>0,\qquad \chi\in C_c^\infty((-\infty,-1)),$$ and suppose that $W\geq0$, $W'\leq0$, and $W''\geq0$ distributionally. For every fixed $\beta>0$, the terminal $u=-\beta W$ has a concave row functional on all profiles with fixed diagonal $Q\in[1/2,2]$. The derivative formula <a href="#eq:src1" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src1">[eq:src1]</a>, continuity of $D_q$ in $L^1$, and the uniform tangent-cap limits hold for this terminal. In particular, the Gaussian interpolation upper bound derived for smooth concave caps applies to $-\beta W$ after removal of the cap.
  - Explanation: The stated compact convex modifications of the quadratic loss retain row-profile concavity, derivative continuity, and cap-removal bounds.
- **claim-vanishing-perturbation-identities** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-press-gg)): Fix $\rho\in(1/4,1/2)$ and put $s_N=N^\rho$. There is an independent centered Gaussian perturbation $H_N^{\rm pert}$ with the following properties.* 1. *Its addition changes the expected pressure by at most $Cs_N^2/N$.* 2. *For the sphere-only system, every subsequential overlap-array limit obtained at almost every perturbation parameter satisfies the Ghirlanda–Guerra identities. With a finite trial cascade, the corresponding identities hold for every continuous function of the pair $(R,Q)$: $$\label{eq:press-joint-gg} \mathbb E\langle f\psi(R_{1,n+1},Q_{1,n+1})\rangle =\frac1n\mathbb E\langle f\rangle\mathbb E\langle\psi(R_{12},Q_{12})\rangle +\frac1n\sum_{\ell=2}^n \mathbb E\langle f\psi(R_{1\ell},Q_{1\ell})\rangle.$$ Here $n\ge2$ and $f$ is a bounded measurable function of the first $n$ joint overlaps. For the sphere-only system, omit $Q$.* 3. *The extraction can be made simultaneously for any prescribed countable collection of systems with finitely many rows removed, and for almost every time in a bounded interpolation parameter interval.* *In (ii)–(iii) the precise extraction convention is this: from any dimension subsequence one can first choose a further subsequence on which all the identity errors vanish for almost every coefficient vector, and then, for each such vector, take any further convergent array subsequence. No assertion is made that averaging limiting arrays over coefficient vectors preserves these identities.
  - Explanation: A subextensive Gaussian perturbation enforces overlap identities along suitably extracted subsequences. The extraction is pointwise in almost every coefficient vector rather than an assertion about mixtures of limiting arrays.
- **claim-overlap-synchronization** (classification, [source](#stmt-lem-press-sync)): Suppose the joint array $(R,Q)$ is a subsequential limit from Lemma <a href="#lem:press-gg" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:press-gg">16</a>. Then $R\ge0$ off the diagonal. There are nonnegative nondecreasing profiles $r,q$, on a common canonical rank array $(U_{\ell\ell'})$, such that $$(R_{\ell\ell'},Q_{\ell\ell'}) \stackrel{\mathrm{law}}{=} (r(U_{\ell\ell'}),q(U_{\ell\ell'})),\qquad\ell\ne\ell'.$$ If the finite trial cascade has prescribed profile $q$, this is that same profile. In the sphere-only case the array is the RPC array determined by its one-overlap marginal.
  - Explanation: The limiting physical and trial overlaps are nonnegative and comonotone on a common rank array. The trial marginal retains its prescribed profile.
- **claim-finite-row-insertion** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-lem-press-row-insertion)): Consider any convergent deleted-row overlap-array subsequence satisfying the preceding lemmas. Reinsert finitely many independent Gaussian rows, with potentials of bounded slope and with covariances given by continuous functions of the available overlap kernels. Suppose those covariances are represented by nondecreasing profiles on the common rank array. Then:* 1. *the entire common-rank genealogy retains its law after insertion;* 2. *conditional on this genealogy, separate inserted row-mark families are independent and have their individually tilted RPC laws;* 3. *for a row of covariance profile $C$, the conditional mean of the product of two terminal derivatives is $D_C(U_{12})$, with diagonal mean $D_{C,d}$.* *The conclusions include convergence of tilted polynomial-growth row observables whenever their requisite moments are uniformly integrable. In particular any convergent rowful array and any further limit with a fixed finite set of its rows removed have the same profile.
  - Explanation: Deleting and reinserting independent bounded-slope Gaussian rows preserves the common genealogy and factors the inserted mark families conditionally on it. Polynomial observables require the stated uniform integrability.
- **claim-empirical-cavity-coefficients** (theorem, [source](#stmt-lem-press-empirical)): Take a subsequence on which the base overlap array converges to profile $q$ and the GG errors for the base, one-row-deleted, and two-row-deleted systems vanish. In every joint array limit, $$\label{eq:src8} \begin{aligned} p_{\ell\ell'}&=\alpha D_q(U_{\ell\ell'}),&&\ell\ne\ell',\\ p_d&=\alpha D_{q,d},\qquad b_N(x^\ell)\longrightarrow b=-p_d+\int_0^1q p_q\,\mathrm ds. \end{aligned}$$ In particular, $\mathbb E\langle\|b_N(x^\ell)-b\|^2\rangle\to0$ along this subsequence.
  - Explanation: Row deletion identifies empirical derivative covariances and the deterministic scalar cavity shift. The scalar shift converges in mean square.
- **claim-gaussian-pressure-formula** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-press-formula)): For Gaussian rows, $u=-\beta V$, and $\alpha>0$, $$\label{eq:src9} P(u)=\min_{q:\,q_*<1}\{\alpha\Phi_u(q)+E(q)\}, \qquad q_*:=\mathop{\mathrm{ess\,sup}}q.$$ Every minimizer of $\mathcal P_u$ has $q_*<1$ and satisfies the spin inverse relations of Section <a href="#sec:hierarchy" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:hierarchy">2</a> with $p=p_q$.
  - Explanation: The Gaussian limiting pressure equals the entropy-form variational minimum. Each minimizing row-spin profile stays strictly below the diagonal and satisfies the spin inverse relation.
- **claim-convex-loss-pressure-support** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-cor-press-convex-loss-upper)): Let $\psi\in C_c^\infty(( -\infty,0))$. There is $w_0>0$, independent of $\beta$, such that for both signs of $w$ with $\|w\|<w_0$ the loss $L_w(z)=V(z)+w\psi(1+z)$ is nonnegative, convex, and nonincreasing. For every fixed $\beta>0$ and every fixed profile $q$ with $q_*<1$, $$\label{eq:press-convex-loss-upper} \limsup_{N\to\infty}P_N(-\beta L_w) \le\alpha\Phi_{-\beta L_w}(q)+E(q).$$ More generally this upper bound holds for any nonpositive, concave, nondecreasing terminal of at most quadratic growth which agrees with a negative quadratic hinge outside a compact set.
  - Explanation: Compact perturbations supported on strictly negative gaps admit a loss-perturbation radius independent of temperature. Interpolation provides a trial pressure upper bound without requiring a perturbed pressure formula.
- **claim-mixture-pressure-universality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thm-univ-pressure)): There is $\varepsilon_0(B_0)>0$, independent of $\beta>0$, with the following property. If $0<\alpha\le B_0$ and $0\le\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0(B_0)$, then $$\lim_{N\to\infty}P_{N,\varepsilon}(u)=P(u).$$ If $q$ is any Gaussian minimizer in <a href="#eq:src9" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src9">[eq:src9]</a> and $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R)$, then, for all sufficiently small $\|d\|$, $$\limsup_{N\to\infty}P_{N,\varepsilon}(u+d\psi) \le \alpha\Phi_{u+d\psi}(q;1)+E(q).$$ The allowed size of $d$ can depend on $\beta,\psi$ and $B_0$.
  - Explanation: A mixture radius chosen independently of temperature preserves the Gaussian pressure and its touching upper supports. The terminal-test perturbation radius may still depend on temperature.
- **claim-residual-variance-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-univ-residual-variance)): Let $q$ be a nonnegative nondecreasing profile with diagonal $1$, and let $u(z)=-\beta(-1-z)_+^2/2$, $\beta>0$. Put $a_0=f_z(0,0)$ for its row solution before the root Gaussian variance. Write $\mathbb E_{u,v}$ for expectation under the tilted endpoint law for profile $vq$ and diagonal $v$. For $1/2\le v\le1$, $$\label{eq:src13} \sqrt v\,\beta\mathbb E_{u,v}(-1-g)_+\le a_0, \qquad \mathbb E_{u,v}(-1-g)_+^2 \le \sqrt{\pi/2}\,\mathbb E_{u,v}(-1-g)_+.$$
  - Explanation: Reducing the diagonal variance controls the tilted first residual moment by the original root derivative and bounds the second moment by an absolute multiple of the first.
- **claim-empirical-row-law** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-univ-observables)): For either the Gaussian law or any mixture in Theorem <a href="#thm:univ-pressure" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thm:univ-pressure">22</a>, at fixed $\beta>0$ and $0<\alpha\le B_0$, $L_N$ converges weakly in probability to $\mu_{\beta,\alpha}$. This measure is atomless, assigns positive mass to $(-\infty,-1)$, and has finite moments of its negative part. The gap and normalized-force observables in the problem have inner $N\to\infty$ limits at every fixed argument, and those limits agree for all these entry laws.
  - Explanation: The empirical projection measure converges in joint probability to an atomless deterministic law. Positive negative-gap mass and moment control justify the configuration-dependent force normalization.
- **claim-pressure-ground-energy-approximation** (bound, [source](#stmt-thresh-pressure-energy)): For every finite $B_0$ there is a constant $C=C(B_0)$ such that, for $N\geq2$, $0\leq M\leq B_0N$, $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1/2$, $\beta>0$, and $0<\delta<1/2$, $$0\leq -\frac{P_{N,\alpha}^{\nu_\varepsilon}(\beta)}{\beta} -\frac1N\mathbb E\min_{\\|y\\|=1}H_A(y) \leq C\delta+\frac1\beta\log\frac C\delta. \label{thresh:eq:pressure-energy}$$ Consequently the Gaussian limit $$e(\alpha)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\mathbb E\min_{\\|y\\|=1}H_A(y) =\lim_{\beta\to\infty} -\frac{P_{\alpha}^{\nu_0}(\beta)}{\beta}$$ exists. On every range where the fixed-temperature pressures agree, the mixture ground-energy limit also exists and equals $e(\alpha)$. Moreover, $e$ is nondecreasing and $1$-Lipschitz, and $e(\alpha)=0$ for $0\leq\alpha\leq1$.
  - Explanation: A spherical-cap estimate approximates minimum energy uniformly by pressure. This yields a common ground-energy limit wherever pressure universality holds, together with monotonicity and Lipschitz continuity.
- **claim-positive-energy-large-density** (bound, [source](#stmt-thresh-large-density)): There is an absolute finite $B>1$ such that the Gaussian ground energy satisfies $e(B)>0$. The same finite-dimensional lower bound used to prove this assertion holds uniformly for $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1/2$.
  - Explanation: At a sufficiently large finite density, a sphere-net argument forces extensive residual energy. Its finite-dimensional estimate also covers the stated variance mixtures.
- **claim-uniform-row-geometry** (bound, [source](#stmt-thresh-uniform-geometry)): Fix $B_0<\infty$ and $0<\rho<1/8$. There are constants $K<\infty$, $c>0$, $u_0>0$, $a>0$, and $C<\infty$, depending only on $(B_0,\rho)$, such that, for all sufficiently large $N$, all $M\leq B_0N$, and every $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1/2$, the following hold simultaneously with probability at least $1-Ce^{-aN}$:* 1. *$\\|A\\|\leq K\sqrt N$;* 2. *for every row set $I$ with $1\leq\|I\|\leq(1-\rho)N$, $$\\|A_I^{\mathsf T}v\\|\geq c\sqrt N\,\\|v\\| \quad\text{for all }v\in\mathbb R^{\|I\|}; \label{thresh:eq:surjection}$$* 3. *every unit $y$ satisfies $$\#\{\mu:\|1+A_\mu y\|\leq u_0\}\leq(1+\rho/2)N. \label{thresh:eq:gap-count}$$
  - Explanation: Uniform random-matrix estimates control the operator norm, right inverses for sufficiently small row sets, and the near-contact count for every unit spin before selecting a minimizer.
- **claim-slab-direction** (construction, [source](#stmt-thresh-slab-direction)): Let $W$ be a $D$-dimensional Euclidean space, $D\geq1$, and $L:W\to\mathbb R^m$ a linear map. There exists a unit $v\in W$ such that $$\\|Lv\\|_\infty\leq\frac{\\|L\\|}{\sqrt D}. \label{thresh:eq:slab-direction}$$
  - Explanation: A finite-dimensional slab argument supplies a unit direction whose individual row projections are controlled by the operator norm and the dimension.
- **claim-deterministic-feasibility-repair** (construction, [source](#stmt-thresh-repair)): Fix $K,c,u_0>0$ and $0<\rho<1/8$. There exists $d_*=d_*(K,c,u_0,\rho)>0$ such that the following holds for all sufficiently large $N$. Suppose $A$ satisfies the first two assertions of Lemma <a href="#thresh:uniform-geometry" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="thresh:uniform-geometry">27</a>, and some unit $y$ satisfies $$\\|r_A(y)\\|\leq d\sqrt N, \qquad S=\{\mu:1+A_\mu y\leq u_0\}, \qquad \|S\|\leq(1-2\rho)N, \quad 0<d\leq d_*.$$ Then there is a unit $\widehat y$ with $1+A_\mu\widehat y\geq0$ for every row $\mu$.
  - Explanation: Under the uniform right-inverse bound, small residual norm, and a strict deficit of problematic rows, successive linear corrections make the gaps feasible. Norm restoration uses radial contraction or an orthogonal kernel displacement as appropriate.
- **claim-deletion-converts-small-energy** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-thresh-deletion)): Let $0<\alpha<\alpha'\leq B_0$, and let the entries have any one of the laws $\nu_\varepsilon$, $0\leq\varepsilon\leq1/2$. If $$\frac1N\mathbb E\min H_{\lfloor\alpha'N\rfloor\times N}\longrightarrow0,$$ then a matrix with $\lfloor\alpha N\rfloor$ rows is satisfiable with probability tending to one.
  - Explanation: Subextensive energy at a strictly higher density implies exact satisfiability at the lower density. Independent random row deletion creates the surplus dimension needed for deterministic repair.
- **claim-sharp-common-threshold** (theorem, [source](#stmt-thresh-sharp)): For Gaussian entries and, with the choice of $B_0$ above, for every fixed $0\leq\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0(B_0)$, the number $\alpha_J$ in <a href="#thresh:eq:threshold-definition" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="thresh:eq:threshold-definition">[thresh:eq:threshold-definition]</a> satisfies $1\leq\alpha_J<\infty$ and $$\lim_{N\to\infty}\mathbb P(\mathrm{SAT})= \begin{cases} 1,&0<\alpha<\alpha_J,\\ 0,&\alpha>\alpha_J. \end{cases}$$ In particular the threshold itself agrees for all these laws. No assertion at $\alpha=\alpha_J$ is needed here.
  - Explanation: The zero-energy threshold is finite and sharp for Gaussian coordinates and the admissible fixed mixtures. The theorem leaves the probability at the threshold itself unspecified.
- **claim-transfer-ordered-limits** (conditional_result, [source](#stmt-thresh-ordered-limits)): Fix $0\leq\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0(B_0)$. On a full interval above the common threshold, the thermodynamic gap and normalized-force observables at every fixed positive temperature and fixed argument agree with their Gaussian counterparts. Consequently each further ordered limit in the problem exists for the mixture law if and only if it exists for the Gaussian law, and their values agree whenever it exists.
  - Explanation: Equality of the inner thermodynamic observable functions transfers each later limit in the specified order. This requires no exchange of limiting operations.
- **claim-unsat-parameter-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-zero-compactness)): For all sufficiently large $\beta$, $$0<c\le\bar\chi_\beta(0)\le C_e, \qquad 0<c_e\le\beta(1-q_{\beta,*})\le C_e. \label{eq:src14}$$ Consequently every sequence $\beta\to\infty$ has a subsequence for which $$\gamma_\beta(t)\,\mathrm dt\ \Longrightarrow\ \gamma(t)\,\mathrm dt+\Delta\delta_1, \qquad \bar\chi(t)=\Delta+\int_t^1\gamma(v)\,\mathrm dv, \qquad L=\bar\chi(0),$$ where $\gamma\ge0$ is nondecreasing and integrable and $\Delta\ge c_e$. The convergence of $\gamma_\beta$ is in $L^1([0,T])$ for every $T<1$, and $\bar\chi_\beta(t)\to\bar\chi(t)$ for $t<1$.
  - Explanation: At fixed positive ground energy, the scaled overlap measures are compact. Their limits retain an integrable monotone interior profile and a positive endpoint mass.
- **claim-zero-temperature-variational-principle** (theorem, [source](#stmt-zero-variational)): For every subsequential limit in Lemma <a href="#zero:compactness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="zero:compactness">33</a>, let $g$ be the solution of $$g_t=-\tfrac12\bigl(g_{zz}+\gamma(t)g_z^2\bigr), \qquad g(1,z)=-\frac{V(z)}{1+\Delta}.$$ It satisfies $$\mathcal E_\alpha(\gamma,\Delta) :=\alpha g(0,0)+\frac12\int_0^1\frac{\mathrm dt}{\bar\chi(t)} =-e, \label{eq:src15}$$ and minimizes this functional over nonnegative nondecreasing integrable $\gamma$ and $\Delta>0$. Here solutions have quadratic growth, nonnegative first derivative, and second derivative in $[-1,0]$; an integrable time coefficient is interpreted by approximation in $L^1$.
  - Explanation: Each extracted zero-temperature profile minimizes the susceptibility functional and recovers the ground energy. The terminal endpoint layer softens the quadratic hinge by its endpoint mass.
- **claim-subsequential-physical-gap** (theorem, [source](#stmt-zero-endpoint)): Let $Z_0=0$ and $\mathrm dZ_t=\gamma(t)g_z(t,Z_t)\,\mathrm dt+\mathrm dB_t$, and put $H=1+Z_1$. Along the subsequence defining $(\gamma,\Delta)$, the tilted row gap converges in distribution to $$h^*=\begin{cases} H,&H\ge0,\\[2pt] H/(1+\Delta),&H<0. \end{cases} \label{eq:src16}$$ Every fixed moment of the negative part converges. Both $H$ and $h^*$ are atomless and assign positive probability to every nonempty open interval. This statement is subsequential; uniqueness is addressed separately below and in Section <a href="#sec:critical" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="sec:critical">8</a>.
  - Explanation: The physical endpoint gap equals the pre-layer gap on its positive side and a contracted gap on its negative side. Negative moments converge, and the fixed-density endpoint laws are atomless.
- **claim-negative-gap-identification** (theorem, [source](#stmt-zero-negative-law)): For every subsequential endpoint law in Proposition <a href="#zero:endpoint" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="zero:endpoint">35</a>, the restriction of the law of $h^*$ to $(-\infty,0)$ is the same. For $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-\infty,0))$, uniformly over Gaussian ground minimizers $y_N$, $$\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^M\psi(1+A_i y_N) \longrightarrow\alpha\mathbb E\psi(h^*) \quad\text{in probability}.$$ Moreover, $$\label{zero:energy-moment} \alpha\mathbb E(h^*)_-^2=2e.$$
  - Explanation: Compact negative-gap tests identify a unique negative marginal across zero-temperature subsequences and all Gaussian ground minimizers. Its quadratic moment equals the ground energy with the stated normalization.
- **claim-endpoint-contact-stability** (bound, [source](#stmt-zero-stability)): For every subsequential zero-temperature optimizer, the contact density parameter $z_c=\alpha\mathbb P(H<0)$ satisfies $$z_c\le(1+1/\Delta)^2. \label{eq:src17}$$
  - Explanation: Overlap-support stability bounds the active contact density in terms of the positive endpoint susceptibility mass.
- **claim-mechanical-contact-count** (bound, [source](#stmt-zero-mechanical)): Almost surely, every positive-energy Gaussian ground minimizer has no zero gap outside its active set $C=\{i:r_i>0\}$, and $k=\|C\|\ge N$. At such a minimizer, $$\label{zero:mechanical-hessian} A_C^T(A_Cy+\mathbf1)=\lambda y, \qquad \lambda=\sum_{i\in C}r_i(1+r_i)>0, \qquad v^T(A_C^TA_C-\lambda I)v\ge0\quad(v\perp y).$$
  - Explanation: Gaussian genericity excludes inactive zero gaps at positive-energy ground minimizers. Tangential Hessian stability forces full active-row rank and the stated contact-count lower bound.
- **claim-negative-cutoff-and-isostaticity** (bound, [source](#stmt-zero-negative-cutoffs)): There are constants $c,C>0$, independent of the density, such that $\alpha\mu\ge c\sqrt e$, where $\mu=\mathbb E(h^*)_-$. At each fixed UNSAT density, uniformly over Gaussian ground minimizers, $$\frac{k}{N}\longrightarrow z_c\quad\text{in probability}.$$ There is $s_0>0$, independent of the density, such that their limiting mean-one force law obeys $F_{\alpha,\infty}(s)\le C/\|\log s\|$ for all $0<s<s_0$, uniformly as $\alpha\downarrow\alpha_J$. Furthermore $z_c\to1$ in this limit, and every weak subsequential jamming force law has total mass one and no atom at zero.
  - Explanation: Uniform small-residual counting preserves active mass and bounds weak normalized forces. The active contact density approaches the isostatic value, and weak jamming force limits retain their mass and mean.
- **claim-uniform-spectral-susceptibility-bounds** (bound, [source](#stmt-zero-spectral)): For every $\varepsilon>0$, with probability tending to one, simultaneously for all row subsets $C$ with $N\le\|C\|\le B_0N$, at least two singular values of $A_C/\sqrt N$ are at most $\sqrt{\|C\|/N}-1+\varepsilon$. Consequently $$\label{zero:susceptibility-bounds} 2e+\alpha\mu\le(\sqrt{z_c}-1)^2\le\Delta^{-2}, \qquad \Delta\le C e^{-1/4}, \qquad \frac1{\sqrt{2e}}\le L\le\frac C{\sqrt e}.$$ In particular $\Delta/L\to0$ as $\alpha\downarrow\alpha_J$.
  - Explanation: Uniform spectral counting over active-row subsets combines with mechanical stability to control the contact density and susceptibility scales. The proof uses the bulk spectral law and concentration rather than an extreme-eigenvalue theorem.
- **claim-normalized-force-cutoffs** (bound, [source](#stmt-zero-normalized-force-cutoff)): For every subsequential endpoint law, put $R=L(h^*)_-$ and $p=\mathbb P(h^*<0)$. There are constants $c,C,u_0>0$, independent of the density, such that throughout the fixed UNSAT interval and for $0<u<u_0$, $$c\le \mathbb ER\le C,\qquad \mathbb P(0<R\le u)\le\frac C{\|\log u\|} \qquad \alpha p\longrightarrow1 \quad(\alpha\downarrow\alpha_J).$$
  - Explanation: Susceptibility normalization keeps the mean residual bounded above and below and preserves a uniform logarithmic cutoff near zero.
- **claim-positive-gap-cutoffs** (bound, [source](#stmt-zero-positive-cutoffs)): Constants $c,C,u_0>0$, independent of the density, exist such that, for $0<\delta<u<1$, $G_{N,\beta,\alpha}(\delta,u)\ge c(u-\delta)$. For every fixed UNSAT density in the interval under consideration and every $0<u<u_0$, $$\label{zero:direct-positive-cutoff} \limsup_{\beta\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty} \mathbb E\left\langle\frac1M\sum_{i=1}^M \mathbf 1_{\{0<h_i\le u\}}\right\rangle \le\frac C{\|\log u\|}$$ with the same constants $C,u_0$ at every such density. In particular every subsequential endpoint law in <a href="#eq:src16" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src16">[eq:src16]</a> satisfies the direct bound $\mathbb P(0<h^*\le u)\le C/\|\log u\|$. The same estimate bounds the ordered zero-temperature and density limsups of $G_{N,\beta,\alpha}(\delta,u)$, uniformly in $0<\delta<u$. The upper bound requires no identification of positive gap tests at exact ground minimizers.
  - Explanation: Positive gaps have a uniform linear lower mass bound and a logarithmic upper cutoff in the prescribed thermal order. The upper estimate is proved on near-ground sublevels, avoiding an unsupported identification of positive tests at exact minimizers.
- **claim-threshold-variational-ratio** (classification, [source](#stmt-zero-threshold-characterization)): With $g$ and $\bar\chi$ as in Proposition <a href="#zero:variational" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="zero:variational">34</a>, $$\label{zero:threshold-ratio} \alpha_J=\inf_{\substack{\gamma\ge0\ \mathrm{nondecreasing},\ \gamma\in L^1\\ \Delta>0}} \frac{\displaystyle\int_0^1\bar\chi(t)^{-1}\,\mathrm dt} {-2g(0,0)}.$$ Equivalently one may impose $\bar\chi(0)=1$ and replace the terminal condition by $g(1,z)=-V(z)/\Delta$.
  - Explanation: The threshold is characterized by an infimum of an entropy-to-row-energy ratio. Scaling gives the equivalent normalized susceptibility formulation.
- **claim-joint-martingale-duality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-duality)): For an original susceptibility $\chi$ with $\Delta>0$, the functional in <a href="#eq:src15" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src15">[eq:src15]</a> equals the minimum over $R\ge0$ in $L^2(\mathcal F_1)$ of $$\label{eq:src18} J_{\alpha,1}(R,s) =\alpha\mathbb E\left[R(1+B_1)+\frac12R^2\right] +\frac\alpha2\left[\frac{c^2}{s(0)} +\int_0^1\frac{\mathbb Eb_t^2}{s(t)}\,\mathrm dt\right] +\frac12\int_0^1s(t)\,\mathrm dt .$$ This minimizer is unique for fixed $s$.
  - Explanation: Terminal quadratic duality expresses the susceptibility functional as a minimum over nonnegative square-integrable terminal forces on Wiener space. The minimizer is unique for a fixed reciprocal susceptibility.
- **claim-perspective-convexity-equality** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-convexity)): The set of admissible $s$ is convex, as is its normalized part $s(0)=1$. The functional $J_{\alpha,\lambda}$ is jointly convex in $(R,s)$. If two pairs attain equality in this convexity inequality at a nontrivial convex combination, then $$\label{crit:perspective-equality} \frac{c_1}{s_1(0)}=\frac{c_2}{s_2(0)},\qquad \frac{b_{1,t}}{s_1(t)}=\frac{b_{2,t}}{s_2(t)} \quad\text{for }\mathrm dt\otimes\mathbb P\text{-almost every }(t,\omega).$$ If $\lambda>0$, equality also forces $R_1=R_2$ in $L^2$.
  - Explanation: Reciprocal susceptibilities form a convex class, and the joint functional is convex by quadratic perspective terms. Equality matches the perspective ratios; a positive terminal quadratic coefficient also identifies the terminal variable.
- **claim-unsat-physical-uniqueness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-unsat-unique)): At each fixed $\alpha>\alpha_c$ the minimizing physical susceptibility in <a href="#eq:src15" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src15">[eq:src15]</a> is unique. Thus the entire zero-temperature endpoint law in <a href="#eq:src16" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src16">[eq:src16]</a>, including its restriction to positive gaps, is unique.
  - Explanation: Strict negative PDE curvature removes the remaining susceptibility degeneracy in the convex equality case. The entire zero-temperature physical endpoint law is consequently unique at fixed UNSAT density.
- **claim-normalized-critical-compactness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-compactness)): The functional $J_{\alpha_c,0}$ is nonnegative on the whole admissible class, without a normalization constraint. Every sequence of normalized physical pairs with $\alpha_n\downarrow\alpha_c$ has a subsequence such that $$\chi_n\to\chi\text{ uniformly on every }[0,T],\ T<1, \qquad R_n\rightharpoonup R\text{ in }L^2(\mathcal F_1).$$ Its limit is normalized, satisfies $s\in L^2(0,1)$ and $c\ge c_0$, and attains $J_{\alpha_c,0}(R,s)=0$.
  - Explanation: Normalized physical pairs approaching the threshold have weak terminal-force and local uniform susceptibility limits. The limiting pair attains the globally nonnegative critical functional at zero.
- **claim-critical-interior-pde** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-pde)): For each subsequence in Proposition <a href="#crit:compactness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="crit:compactness">47</a>, $f_n$ and $a_n$ converge locally uniformly on $[0,1)\times\mathbb R$ to functions $f$ and $a=f_h$ determined by $\chi$. They satisfy <a href="#eq:src20" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src20">[eq:src20]</a> with $\lambda_n+\chi_n$ replaced by $\chi$. They are smooth in the spatial variable in the interior and locally Lipschitz in time there, together with each spatial derivative used below. For $t<1$, $$f_{hh}(t,h)<0,\qquad f_{hhh}(t,h)>0, \qquad \lim_{h\to+\infty}a(t,h)=0.$$ On the common Wiener space the limiting martingale and diffusion obey $$\label{eq:src21} H_t=1+B_t+\int_0^t\gamma(v)r_v\,\mathrm dv, \qquad r_t=a(t,H_t),\qquad b_t=f_{hh}(t,H_t),\qquad t<1.$$ Both $H_t$ and $r_t$ extend continuously and in $L^2$ to $t=1$, with $r_1=R$.
  - Explanation: The critical susceptibility determines the interior PDE and the coupled forward diffusion. Strict spatial curvature, temporal regularity, and martingale identification persist up to continuous square-integrable endpoint extensions.
- **claim-critical-pair-uniqueness** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-unique-critical)): Any two subsequential limits supplied by Proposition <a href="#crit:compactness" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="crit:compactness">47</a> coincide on the common Wiener space. In particular the normalized susceptibility and the law of $(H_1,R)$ are independent of the density sequence.
  - Explanation: Convex equality identifies normalized curvatures along the states. Common Brownian noise and the positive common martingale mean then force the normalized critical pairs to coincide.
- **claim-critical-first-order-conditions** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-kkt)): The critical pair satisfies $$\begin{gathered} H_1+\Delta R\ge0,\qquad R(H_1+\Delta R)=0 \quad\text{almost surely}, \label{crit:complementarity}\\ K(t)\ge0\quad(0\le t\le1),\qquad \int_0^1\gamma(t)J(t)\,\mathrm dt=\int_{[0,1)}K(t)\,\nu(\mathrm dt)=0. \label{crit:kkt-profile} \end{gathered}$$ The profile $\gamma$ vanishes on an initial interval. At every interior point of $\mathop{\mathrm{supp}}\nu$ one has $J=0$ and $J'\le0$; at every non-isolated such point, $J'=0$. Finally $J(1)=0$.
  - Explanation: Optimality gives terminal complementarity, a nonnegative integrated profile defect, and vanishing variation on the increase support. The increase profile starts with a zero interval and its terminal defect vanishes.
- **claim-vanishing-critical-endpoint** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-no-endpoint)): The critical susceptibility satisfies $\Delta=0$. Its increase measure $\nu$ accumulates at $1$, and with $k=-\chi f_{hh}$ one has, at every interior support point, $$\label{eq:src22} \alpha_c\mathbb Ek(t,H_t)=1+\alpha_c c\chi(t), \qquad \alpha_c\mathbb Ek(t,H_t)^2\le1.$$ The second inequality is an equality at non-isolated interior support points.
  - Explanation: The critical endpoint susceptibility is zero. The increase support reaches arbitrarily late times, with normalized-curvature moment identities at its interior points.
- **claim-strong-critical-convergence** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-strong)): As $\alpha_n\downarrow\alpha_c$, the normalized physical variables satisfy $$R_n\to R\text{ in }L^2,\qquad \gamma_n\to\gamma\text{ in }L^1(0,1),\qquad H_{n,1}\to H_1\text{ in }L^2.$$ The physical endpoint gap is $h_n^*=H_{n,1}+\chi_n(1)R_n$, its residual is $(h_n^*)_-=\lambda_nR_n$, and $h_n^*\to H_1\ge0$ in $L^2$.
  - Explanation: A rescaled critical trial upgrades weak terminal convergence to strong convergence and makes the profile convergence global. The physical gap converges strongly to a nonnegative critical gap.
- **claim-critical-contact-mass** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-contacts)): At the critical pair, $$\mathbb P(R>0)=\mathbb P(H_1=0)=\frac1{\alpha_c}, \qquad \{R>0\}=\{H_1=0\}\quad\text{modulo null sets}.$$
  - Explanation: Uniform force and gap cutoffs preserve positivity probabilities through strong convergence. Critical contacts are exactly the zero-gap event modulo null sets, with the stated mass.
- **claim-no-positive-endpoint-atoms** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-no-positive-atoms)): Neither $R$ nor $H_1$ has an atom at any strictly positive point.
  - Explanation: The terminal gap and residual force have no atoms at strictly positive values. This assertion does not by itself assert the existence or continuity of a density.
- **claim-ordered-critical-observables** (theorem, [source](#stmt-crit-ordered-laws)): The Gaussian observables in the problem have all their stated ordered limits, at every $u>0$ and $s>0$, and are given by $$\label{crit:limiting-laws} G_J(u)=\mathbb P(0<H_1\le u),\qquad F_J(s)=\mathbb P\left(\frac{R}{\alpha_c c}\le s\,\middle\|\,R>0\right).$$ The force law has mean one and no atom at zero. These limiting laws are also the laws for all Gaussian scale mixtures in the fixed-temperature comparison range. More explicitly, for every $0<\delta<u$ and $s>0$, the individual limits at each level of $$\begin{gathered} \lim_{\alpha\downarrow\alpha_c}\lim_{\beta\to\infty} \lim_{N\to\infty}G_{N,\beta,\alpha}(\delta,u) =\mathbb P(\delta<H_1\le u),\\ \lim_{\alpha\downarrow\alpha_c}\lim_{\beta\to\infty} \lim_{N\to\infty}F_{N,\beta,\alpha}(s) =F_J(s) \end{gathered}$$ exist; the additional limit $\delta\downarrow0$ in the first line gives $G_J(u)$.
  - Explanation: The successive microscopic limits identify positive gaps and the conditioned mean-one force law from the critical pair. The lower gap cutoff is removed only after the density limit, and the admissible mixtures share these laws.
- **claim-pointwise-critical-barriers** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-scale-barriers)): For $z=h/\sqrt\tau$, $$\label{eq:src23} \sqrt\tau\,[\phi(z)-z\Phi(-z)]\le m(t,h) \le\sqrt\tau\,\frac{\phi(z)}{\Phi(z)}.$$ Consequently, with fixed positive constants $C,c_0$, $$\label{eq:src24} k(t,h)\le C e^{-c_0z^2}\quad(z\ge1),\qquad l(t,h)\le C\|z\|^{-2}\quad(z\le-1),\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}kl\,\mathrm dh\le C\sqrt\tau.$$
  - Explanation: Heat and normal-tail barriers bound the force field pointwise. Secants give the positive and negative curvature tails and an integrable transition-layer bound.
- **claim-subpower-scale-ratio** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-scale-subpower)): As $\tau\downarrow0$, $$\label{eq:src25} \log D=o(\|\log\tau\|).$$
  - Explanation: The scale ratio cannot diverge at any fixed algebraic rate as the endpoint is approached. The estimate extends across affine gaps of the increase support.
- **claim-strict-reciprocal-power-improvement** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-scale-strict-power)): There exist $\eta>0$ and $C<\infty$ such that $s(\tau)\le C\tau^{-1/2+\eta}$. In particular $w(\tau)\le C\tau^{2\eta}$.
  - Explanation: Inverse-flow estimates improve reciprocal susceptibility growth strictly beyond the endpoint integrability boundary and give decay of the remaining variance time.
- **claim-martingale-bin-comparison** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-scale-bins)): Under these assumptions there exist $0<u_0<T$ and finite constants $C,P$, depending on the process and the constants $c_a$, such that $M_j(u):=\mathbb P(j\sqrt u\le Z_{T-u}\le(j+1)\sqrt u)$ satisfies $$\label{eq:src27} M_j(u)\le Cj^P M_1(u),\qquad j\ge2,\quad 0<u\le u_0.$$
  - Explanation: Conditional Brownian steering compares remote moving bins with the first positive bin by a polynomial factor, without requiring the martingale itself to be Markov.
- **claim-bounded-natural-scale-ratio** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-scale-bounded-d)): There is a constant $C$ such that $1\le D\le C$ near the endpoint. Consequently $w\asymp\tau/\chi^2$ and $\int_t^1s\asymp\tau/\chi$.
  - Explanation: The natural force and gap spatial scales are uniformly comparable near the endpoint. This also controls the remaining integral of reciprocal susceptibility.
- **claim-endpoint-window-masses** (bound, [source](#stmt-prop-scale-endpoint-masses)): There exist $t_1<1$ and constants $0<c_1<C_1<\infty$ such that, for every $t_1<t<1$, $$\label{eq:src31} \mathbb P(0<R\le\sqrt w)\asymp\chi(t),\qquad \mathbb P(0<Y\le\sqrt\tau)\asymp\chi(t).$$ Both comparisons use the same fixed constants $c_1,C_1$, after enlarging their range if necessary; the time $t$ need not be a support point.
  - Explanation: Strictly positive force and gap masses in their respective shrinking windows are both comparable to susceptibility. The windows exclude endpoint atoms, and the result holds between support points as well.
- **claim-inverse-slope-barriers** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-scale-inverse-slope)): At every interior critical time, $$\label{eq:src32} \frac97 k(1-k)^{3/2}\le V\le\frac65[k(1-k)]^{3/4}.$$
  - Explanation: Explicit stationary comparison functions bound the rescaled inverse slope throughout the interior critical layer.
- **claim-weighted-curvature-positivity** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-scale-curvature)): There is $c_1>0$ such that, at all sufficiently late times, with $A_0=\tau\gamma/\chi\in[0,1]$, $$\label{eq:src33} \mathbb E\!\left[V_z^2+6A_0(2k-1)V^2+6A_0^2k^2(1-k)^2\right] \ge c_1p_t(0)\sqrt\tau.$$
  - Explanation: A cumulative unweighted curvature inequality remains strictly positive against the limiting decreasing density. Compactness transfers this positivity uniformly to late critical times.
- **claim-terminal-full-increase-support** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-scale-full-support)): The increase support of $\gamma$ contains a terminal interval $(t_*,1)$. On this interval $J=J'=0$, and $\gamma$ has a continuous version with $$\label{eq:src34} A_0=\frac{\mathbb EV^2}{2\mathbb Ek^2(1-k)}.$$
  - Explanation: Strict curvature excludes late affine gaps of susceptibility. On the resulting full-support terminal interval, the profile defect vanishes and an integral quotient gives a continuous increase coefficient.
- **claim-entire-logarithmic-limits** (construction, [source](#stmt-lem-contr-entire)): Every sequence $u_n\to\infty$ has a subsequence along which the translated rescaled profiles converge locally to a solution of <a href="#eq:src35" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src35">[eq:src35]</a> for all $u\in\mathbb R$. The limiting coefficient $A$ is continuous and takes values in $[0,1]$. The value barriers <a href="#eq:src23" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src23">[eq:src23]</a>, the inverse-curvature bounds <a href="#eq:src32" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src32">[eq:src32]</a>, and the Gaussian bounds for $k$ on the positive half-line, $l$ on the negative half-line, and $V,V_z$ on both half-lines hold uniformly in entire time. Moreover $P>0$, $P\le C\exp(C\|z\|)$, and on every bounded spatial interval $P$ has a positive lower bound independent of entire time. The limits satisfy $$\int_\mathbb RMXP\,\mathrm dz=\int_\mathbb RklP\,\mathrm dz=c, \qquad A=\frac{\displaystyle\int_\mathbb RV^2P\,\mathrm dz} {\displaystyle2\int_\mathbb Rk^2lP\,\mathrm dz}, \label{eq:src36}$$ where $c=\mathbb ER>0$ is the critical normalization constant.
  - Explanation: Translations in logarithmic endpoint time have entire subsequential limits preserving the barriers, positive density control, and critical integral identities. The limiting coefficient is continuous.
- **claim-entire-coefficient-reduction** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-contr-a)): Every entire limit in Lemma <a href="#lem:contr-entire" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="lem:contr-entire">65</a> has $0\le A\le0.41$.
  - Explanation: A certified positive cumulative functional rules out excessive coefficient values at a maximum of an entire limit.
- **claim-heat-reference-curvature-ratio** (bound, [source](#stmt-lem-contr-heat-ratio)): For every input, at the same $k\in(0,1)$, $$\sqrt{1-0.82\cdot1.12} \ \le\ \frac{V_i}{W_0} \ \le\ \sqrt{1+0.82\cdot0.13}, \qquad W_0(k)=\phi(\Phi^{-1}(k)). \label{eq:src43}$$ Consequently the ratio of any two input curvatures is less than $3.8$.
  - Explanation: Each input curvature is uniformly comparable with the heat reference at equal slope. These bounds also give the stated comparison between any pair of input curvatures.
- **claim-entire-limit-rigidity** (theorem, [source](#stmt-prop-contr-rigidity)): Let $(M_i,P_i,A)$ be a density input as defined in Subsection <a href="#subsec:contr-comparisons" data-reference-type="ref" data-reference="subsec:contr-comparisons">10.4</a>, and suppose that the two identities <a href="#eq:contr-homogeneous" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:contr-homogeneous">[eq:contr-homogeneous]</a> hold at every entire time. Then $A\equiv a_*$. In particular every entire limit of the critical rescaled profiles has this coefficient, and $$\lim_{\tau\downarrow0}\frac{\tau\gamma(\tau)}{\chi(\tau)}=a_*, \qquad \lim_{\tau\downarrow0}\frac{\log\chi(\tau)}{\log\tau}=a_*.$$ The root of $\lambda(a)=a$ in the certified interval is unique.
  - Explanation: Reference barriers and signed integral tests first narrow the coefficient range. A strict local contraction then identifies every admissible entire critical coefficient with the certified spectral root, yielding the susceptibility logarithmic power and root uniqueness in the certified interval.
- **claim-stationary-profile-error** (bound, [source](#stmt-cert-m-error)): For every certified rational parameter, $$\\|M_a-\widetilde M\\|_{L^\infty([-24,24])}<10^{-22},\qquad \\|M_a'-\widetilde M'\\|_{L^\infty([-24,24])}<4\cdot10^{-20}.$$
  - Explanation: Integer residual and boundary tests, followed by maximum-principle and integrating-factor estimates, bound the stationary approximation and its derivative relative to the exact profile.
- **claim-riccati-tail-enclosure** (bound, [source](#stmt-cert-tail-enclosure)): For $x\ge12$, the polynomial-order branch is uniquely determined by $$T(x)-Kx^{-7}\le S_\varepsilon(x)\le T(x)+Kx^{-7}.$$ It depends continuously on $\lambda$ within each trial window. Moreover, $$\label{cert:tail-derivatives} \|S_\varepsilon(x)\|<.071,\qquad \|xS_\varepsilon'(x)+S_\varepsilon(x)\|<.0055.$$
  - Explanation: Explicit asymptotic barriers uniquely select the polynomial-order logarithmic derivative at infinity and control its magnitude and derivative. The branch depends continuously on the trial eigenvalue.

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-hier-rank-array",
        "exact_quote": "For two independent samples from a depth-$k$ cascade, the probability that their leaves share exactly $j$ edges is $w_j$, $0\\le j\\le k$; sharing $k$ edges includes selecting the same leaf.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-hier-array-continuity",
        "exact_quote": "Let $G_n$ be random probability measures. Suppose that the jointly sampled arrays of a finite list of uniformly bounded positive-semidefinite kernels, and any other bounded observables being retained, converge in law on every finite set of replicas. Conditional on these arrays, adjoin independent centered Gaussian fields with the prescribed kernels. Let $X_n$ be the evaluation of one fixed continuous function on the retained single-replica variables and those fields, and assume, for every fixed $a>0$, $$\\sup_n\\mathbb EG_n(e^{a|X_n|})<\\infty.\n \\label{eq:hier-exponential-moments}$$ Then the expectations of $\\log G_n(e^{X_n})$, and the expectations of bounded continuous functions of finitely many replicas sampled from $e^{X_n}G_n/G_n(e^{X_n})$, converge to the corresponding functionals of the limiting array. Independent auxiliary variables of a fixed law may be adjoined to each replica. The conclusion also holds for unbounded observables whose truncation errors vanish uniformly under the tilted law; in particular this follows for polynomial functions of the Gaussian fields under <a href=\"#eq:hier-exponential-moments\" data-reference-type=\"eqref\" data-reference=\"eq:hier-exponential-moments\">[eq:hier-exponential-moments]</a>.",
        "source_id": "PM-222.2"
      },

        "anchor": "stmt-prop-hier-spherical-limit",
        "exact_quote": "The limit $\\mathcal S(p)=\\lim_{N\\to\\infty}\\mathcal S_N(p)$ exists and is uniform over all nonnegative nondecreasing profiles bounded by any fixed constant. For a finite-step profile without residual diagonal, put $$\\Delta p_j=p_j-p_{j-1},\\qquad\n I=\\sum_{j=1}^k m_{j-1}\\Delta p_j,\n \\qquad\n \\lambda_j=b-\\sum_{i=j+1}^k m_{i-1}\\Delta p_i\\quad(0\\le j\\le k).$$ Thus $\\lambda_k=b$, $\\lambda_0=b-I$, and $\\lambda_{j-1}=\\lambda_j-m_{j-1}\\Delta p_j$. Define, for $b>I$, $$X(b)=-\\frac12\\log b+\\frac{p_0}{2\\lambda_0}\n       +\\sum_{j=1}^k\\frac1{2m_{j-1}}\n                         \\log\\frac{\\lambda_j}{\\lambda_{j-1}}.\n \\label{eq:hier-gaussian-spin}$$ There is exactly one $b>I$ satisfying $$-2X'(b)=\\frac1b+\\frac{p_0}{\\lambda_0^2}\n       +\\sum_{j=1}^k\\frac{p_j-p_{j-1}}{\\lambda_j\\lambda_{j-1}}=1.\n \\label{eq:src2}$$ At this value of $b$, $$\\mathcal S(p)=X(b)+\\frac b2-\\frac12-\\frac{p_k}{2}.\n \\label{eq:hier-spherical-value}$$ If $p\\le B$, its saddle point satisfies $1\\le b<2(B+1)$.",

        "exact_quote": "The functional $\\mathcal S$ is concave on bounded nonnegative nondecreasing profiles.         "anchor": "stmt-prop-hier-entropy-conjugacy",
        "exact_quote": "Let $q$ be nonnegative and nondecreasing with $q_*<1$, and use $\\chi_q$ defined above. Then the following supremum is attained: $$\\begin{split}\n E(q)&:=\\sup_{\\substack{p\\ge0\\text{ bounded}\\\\p\\text{ nondecreasing}}}\n       \\left\\{\\mathcal S(p)+\\frac12\\int_0^1q(s)p(s)\\,\\mathrm ds\\right\\}\\\\\n &=\\frac12\\left\\{\\log(1-q_*)+\n                       \\int_0^{q_*}\\frac{\\mathrm dt}{\\chi_q(t)}\\right\\},\n \\qquad \\chi_q(t)=\\int_t^1m_q(v)\\,\\mathrm dv.\n \\end{split}\n \\label{eq:src3}$$ An optimizer may be chosen with $p_*\\le q_*/(1-q_*)^2$. Equivalently, $$E(q)=\\frac12\\int_0^1\n       \\left\\{\\frac1{\\chi_q(t)}-\\frac1{1-t}\\right\\}\\,\\mathrm dt,\n \\label{eq:hier-entropy-integral}$$ where the integrand is identically zero for $t>q_*$. For profiles $q,\\widetilde q\\le Q<1$, $$|E(q)-E(\\widetilde q)|\n \\le\\frac{Q}{2(1-Q)^2}\\|q-\\widetilde q\\|_1.\n \\label{eq:hier-entropy-continuity}$$",
        "source_id": "PM-222.2"
      },
      "evidence": [
        {
          "anchor": "stmt-prop-hier-entropy-conjugacy",

        "anchor": "stmt-lem-press-gg",
        "exact_quote": "Fix $\\rho\\in(1/4,1/2)$ and put $s_N=N^\\rho$.         "anchor": "stmt-lem-press-row-insertion",
        "exact_quote": "Consider any convergent deleted-row overlap-array subsequence satisfying the preceding lemmas. Reinsert finitely many independent Gaussian rows, with potentials of bounded slope and with covariances given by continuous functions of the available overlap kernels. Suppose those covariances are represented by nondecreasing profiles on the common rank array. Then:*\n\n1.  *the entire common-rank genealogy retains its law after insertion;*\n\n2.  *conditional on this genealogy, separate inserted row-mark families are independent and have their individually tilted RPC laws;*\n\n3.  *for a row of covariance profile $C$, the conditional mean of the product of two terminal derivatives is $D_C(U_{12})$, with diagonal mean $D_{C,d}$.*\n\n*The conclusions include convergence of tilted polynomial-growth row observables whenever their requisite moments are uniformly integrable. <a id="pm-s2"></a>
## 2. Definitions, validity and bounds

- **spherical configuration space** ([source](#pm-h-4)): On $$\mathbb S_N=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:\\|x\\|^2=N\}$$ use normalized surface measure $\sigma_N$.
- **projection, gap, quadratic penalty, and Hamiltonian** ([source](#pm-h-4)): For $y=x/\sqrt N$, define $$\label{eq:intro-model} g_\mu(x)=A_\mu y,\qquad h_\mu(x)=1+g_\mu(x),\qquad V(z)=\frac12(-1-z)_+^2,\qquad H_N(x)=\sum_{\mu=1}^M V(g_\mu(x)).$$
- **SAT and UNSAT** ([source](#pm-h-4)): The realization is satisfiable (SAT) if $H_N$ vanishes somewhere on $\mathbb S_N$ and is unsatisfiable (UNSAT) otherwise.
- **positive-gap observable** ([source](#pm-h-4)): For $0<\delta<u$, put $$\label{eq:intro-gap-observable} G_{N,\beta,\alpha}(\delta,u) =\mathbb E\left\langle\frac1M\sum_{\mu=1}^M \mathbf 1\{\delta<h_\mu(x)\le u\}\right\rangle.$$
- **mean-normalized force observable** ([source](#pm-h-4)): and set $$\label{eq:intro-force-observable} F_{N,\beta,\alpha}(s)= \mathbb E\left\langle\frac1{\|C(x)\|}\sum_{\mu\in C(x)} \mathbf 1\{f_\mu(x)\le s\}\right\rangle,\qquad s>0.$$
- **ordered jamming limits** ([source](#eq:intro-order)): All limits at jamming are taken from UNSAT in the order $$\label{eq:intro-order} \lim_{\alpha\downarrow\alpha_c}\ \lim_{\beta\to\infty}\ \lim_{N\to\infty}.$$
- **Gaussian variance-mixture coordinate law** ([source](#pm-h-4)): The perturbations considered here have coordinate law $$\label{eq:intro-mixture} \nu_\varepsilon=\tfrac12\mathcal N(0,1-\varepsilon)+\tfrac12\mathcal N(0,1+\varepsilon),\qquad 0\le\varepsilon<1,$$ where the second argument is the variance.
- **monotone covariance profiles** ([source](#pm-h-9)): Let $\mathcal Q_Q$ be the set of nonnegative nondecreasing functions $q:[0,1)\to[0,Q]$, identified up to Lebesgue-null sets.
- **terminal convolution** ([source](#pm-h-10)): When $q_k<Q$, replace $e^{u(z)}$ at a leaf by $\mathbb E_G e^{u(z+\sqrt{Q-q_k}\,G)}$, where $G\sim\mathcal N(0,1)$.
- **row functional** ([source](#pm-h-10)): Define $$\Phi_u(q;Q)=\mathbb E\log\sum_\tau v_\tau e^{u(z_\tau)}.$$
- **overlap distribution and integrated distribution** ([source](#pm-h-12)): For any nonnegative nondecreasing $v$ with $v_*<1$, define its overlap distribution and integrated distribution by $$m_v(t)=\mathbb P(v(U)\le t),\qquad \chi_v(t)=\int_t^1m_v(a)\,\mathrm da, \qquad U\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1].$$
- **ground residual norm** ([source](#sec:threshold)): Set $$r_A(y)=(-\mathbf 1-Ay)_+,\qquad H_A(y)=\frac12\\|r_A(y)\\|_2^2,\qquad R(A)=\min_{\\|y\\|_2=1}\\|r_A(y)\\|_2.$$
- **energetic threshold** ([source](#thresh:eq:threshold-definition)): Define $$\alpha_J=\sup\{\alpha\geq0:e(\alpha)=0\}. \label{thresh:eq:threshold-definition}$$
- **admissible susceptibility** ([source](#pm-h-51)): An admissible susceptibility is $$\chi(t)=\Delta+\int_t^1\gamma(v)\,\mathrm dv, \qquad \Delta\ge0,\qquad \chi(t)>0\quad(t<1),$$ where $\gamma\ge0$ is nondecreasing and belongs to $L^1(0,1)$.
- **admissible terminal-force pair** ([source](#pm-h-51)): A pair $(R,s)$ is admissible when its susceptibility is admissible and $R\ge0$ almost surely belongs to $L^2(\mathcal F_1)$.
- **joint martingale functional** ([source](#pm-h-51)): For $\lambda\ge0$ define the joint functional $$\label{crit:def-functional} \begin{split} J_{\alpha,\lambda}(R,s) ={}&\alpha\mathbb E\left[R(1+B_1)+\frac\lambda2R^2\right] +\frac\alpha2\left\{\frac{c^2}{s(0)} +\int_0^1\frac{\mathbb Eb_t^2}{s(t)}\,\mathrm dt\right\} +\frac12\int_0^1s(t)\,\mathrm dt . \end{split}$$
- **density input for entire comparisons** ([source](#subsec:contr-comparisons)): A density input also includes a positive function $P_i(u,z)$ whose logarithmic slope $Q_i=(\log P_i)_z$ is bounded on $\mathbb R^2$, nonpositive, and satisfies <a href="#eq:src37" data-reference-type="eqref" data-reference="eq:src37">[eq:src37]</a>, with $u=-v$.

<a id="pm-s3"></a>
## 3. Proof roadmap

- **step-cascade-foundations** [claim](#stmt-lem-hier-cascade-tilt) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hier-cascade-tilt): Poisson marking and stable-sum moments establish normalization, genealogy invariance, and independent-family factorization. -> A normalized cascade and explicit tilted transitions for hierarchical marks.
- **step-rank-array-and-continuity** [claim](#stmt-lem-hier-array-continuity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-hier-array-continuity): Nested partition sampling constructs the rank array; clipping tilt weights and polynomial approximation pass finite-replica convergence to logarithms and tilted observables. -> Common-rank representations and continuity of the tilted row functional.
- **step-spherical-entropy** [claim](#stmt-prop-hier-spherical-limit) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-hier-spherical-limit): Evaluate the Gaussian spin integral, select its variance-normalizing saddle point, compare a typical radial shell with the sphere, and use profile compactness. -> Explicit uniform spherical limit, concavity, inverse supergradient map, and attained entropy conjugate.
- **step-row-regularity-and-hessian** [claim](#stmt-lem-conc-hessian) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-conc-hessian): Parabolic comparison establishes growth and curvature bounds; differentiated equations and integration by parts give the modified Hessian identity. -> A well-posed row PDE with justified variations and an exact Hessian formula.
- **step-row-concavity-and-cap-removal** [claim](#stmt-cor-conc-hinge-stability) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cor-conc-hinge-stability): Rewrite the Hessian as negative squares, obtain uniform diffusion mass in a curvature interval, compare compact perturbations, and remove regularizations in the stated order. -> Concavity and strict stability for the uncapped hinge, plus concavity and cap limits for the stated convex loss perturbations.
- **step-overlap-extraction-and-row-insertion** [claim](#stmt-lem-press-sync) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-press-sync): A vanishing Gaussian perturbation gives pointwise subsequential overlap identities; ultrametricity and positivity synchronize profiles, and Gaussian row insertion preserves the common genealogy. -> Admissible synchronized cavity arrays and conditionally independent inserted row families.
- **step-pressure-and-touching-supports** [claim](#stmt-prop-press-formula) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-press-formula): Concavity signs the upper interpolation; empirical cavity coefficients and spherical dimension increments supply the lower bound. Strict monotonicity identifies the minimizing profile with the spin response. -> Gaussian entropy-form pressure and touching upper supports for both terminal-test signs and the stated convex loss perturbations.
- **step-mixture-universality-and-row-laws** [claim](#stmt-thm-univ-pressure) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-univ-residual-variance): Replace small coordinates by moment matching, localize large coordinates, and compare their entropy cost with variance gains using temperature-independent residual estimates. Differentiate touching supports to identify empirical rows. -> A common fixed-temperature pressure, empirical row law, and correctly normalized gap and force observables.
- **step-ground-energy-and-uniform-geometry** [claim](#stmt-thresh-uniform-geometry) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thresh-uniform-geometry): Spherical-cap pressure bounds define the ground energy; net arguments give positive energy at a finite density and uniform operator, surjection, and gap-count bounds. -> A common energetic threshold and random-matrix geometry valid before choosing a minimizer.
- **step-repair-and-sharp-threshold** [claim](#stmt-thresh-sharp) / [proof](#proof-stmt-thresh-sharp): Random deletion reduces the problematic-row count; successive right-inverse corrections repair gaps, and a slab direction restores norm when needed. Residual concentration proves infeasibility above threshold. -> Sharp common SAT threshold and transfer of later ordered limits.
- **step-zero-temperature-extraction** [claim](#stmt-zero-variational) / [proof](#proof-stmt-zero-variational): Compactness separates the integrable interior profile from its endpoint mass. A first-order terminal comparison identifies the variational limit and the physical proximal gap. -> Zero-temperature minimizing pairs, subsequential endpoint laws, unique negative marginal, and endpoint stability.
- **step-mechanical-and-spectral-cutoffs** [claim](#stmt-zero-spectral) / [proof](#proof-stmt-zero-spectral): Gaussian genericity and tangential Hessian positivity force active-row rank. Conditional-gradient counting controls weak residuals, while bulk spectral concentration bounds all active subsets. -> Mechanical contact count, uniform negative cutoffs, susceptibility bounds, and normalized-force cutoff control.
- **step-positive-cutoff-and-threshold-ratio** [claim](#stmt-zero-positive-cutoffs) / [proof](#proof-stmt-zero-positive-cutoffs): Control tangent gradients and active counts on thin near-ground sublevels before concentrating Gibbs mass. Scaling variational trials gives the normalized threshold ratio. -> Positive-gap cutoff estimates in the required order and the variational threshold characterization.
- **step-martingale-convexity-and-unsat-uniqueness** [claim](#stmt-crit-duality) / [proof](#proof-stmt-crit-duality): Quadratic terminal duality represents the PDE by a nonnegative terminal martingale. Perspective convexity and strict interior curvature identify equality cases. -> Joint convexity and uniqueness of the full physical endpoint law at fixed UNSAT density.
- **step-critical-compactness-and-uniqueness** [claim](#stmt-crit-unique-critical) / [proof](#proof-stmt-crit-unique-critical): Normalize initial susceptibility, extract weak terminal limits on the common space, recover the interior PDE, and use common-noise curvature matching to identify the limit. -> A unique normalized physical critical pair with interior diffusion and martingale representation.
- **step-critical-endpoint-and-strong-convergence** [claim](#stmt-crit-strong) / [proof](#proof-stmt-crit-strong): First-order cone and profile variations give complementarity and support conditions. These exclude a positive endpoint susceptibility; rescaled critical trials then control the terminal norm. -> Vanishing critical endpoint susceptibility and strong convergence of terminal forces, profiles, and physical gaps.
- **step-contact-masses-and-ordered-laws** [claim](#stmt-crit-ordered-laws) / [proof](#proof-stmt-crit-ordered-laws): Uniform small-force and positive-gap cutoffs preserve contact probabilities. Local nondegeneracy and bounded drift away from contact exclude positive atoms, enabling every positive cutoff. -> Identified contact mass and the prescribed ordered gap and mean-one force laws, common to the admissible mixtures.
- **step-critical-scale-control** [claim](#stmt-prop-scale-bounded-d) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-scale-bounded-d): Pointwise heat barriers and inverse-flow densities first exclude algebraic scale divergence. A strict reciprocal-power improvement and conditional martingale bin comparison then bound the ratio uniformly. -> Pointwise barriers, subpower and strict-power estimates, bin comparison, and bounded natural scale ratio.
- **step-endpoint-masses-and-full-support** [claim](#stmt-prop-scale-full-support) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-scale-full-support): Density comparison and martingale windows identify endpoint masses. Inverse-slope barriers imply a strictly positive weighted curvature inequality, excluding terminal support gaps. -> Two-sided force and gap window masses, inverse-slope bounds, curvature positivity, and full terminal increase support.
- **step-entire-limits-and-coefficient-reduction** [claim](#stmt-lem-contr-a) / [proof](#proof-stmt-lem-contr-a): Translate logarithmic endpoint time and use local parabolic compactness with uniform tails. A signed cumulative curvature bound reduces the entire coefficient range. -> Entire density inputs with homogeneous critical identities and the reduced coefficient range.
- **step-certified-reference-and-tail-errors** [claim](#stmt-cert-m-error) / [proof](#proof-stmt-cert-m-error): Integer residuals and boundary tests control the stationary approximation. Riccati tail barriers select the square-integrable spectral branch and inward shooting encloses the eigenvalue. -> Certified stationary errors, unique Riccati tails, and opposite spectral signs at the root bracket endpoints.
- **step-local-rigidity-and-exponents** [claim](#stmt-prop-contr-rigidity) / [proof](#proof-stmt-prop-contr-rigidity): Reference comparisons enclose inverse-coordinate signed functionals. Successive coefficient reductions enter a local regime where the functional derivative bound is strictly contractive; compactness transfers rigidity to the microscopic critical layer. -> Selected susceptibility power, uniqueness of the certified root, cumulative exponent laws, and their exact relation.

          "anchor": "stmt-lem-press-gg",
          "exact_quote": "Fix $\\rho\\in(1/4,1/2)$ and put $s_N=N^\\rho$. With a finite trial cascade, the corresponding identities hold for every continuous function of the pair $(R,Q)$: $$\\label{eq:press-joint-gg}\n     \\mathbb E\\langle f\\psi(R_{1,n+1},Q_{1,n+1})\\rangle\n     =\\frac1n\\mathbb E\\langle f\\rangle\\mathbb E\\langle\\psi(R_{12},Q_{12})\\rangle\n      +\\frac1n\\sum_{\\ell=2}^n\n       \\mathbb E\\langle f\\psi(R_{1\\ell},Q_{1\\ell})\\rangle.$$ Here $n\\ge2$ and $f$ is a bounded measurable function of the first $n$ joint overlaps.
